title: Why Experiments Lie
editorial_note: Automated dialogue draft from the revised lesson. Review spoken wording and meaning before publishing.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Today we're talking about Why Experiments Lie. By the end, you'll know why this matters, how to use it, and what to notice in a real product.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the problem we are trying to understand?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Before launch, threats include a vague hypothesis, variants that differ in several mechanisms, underpowered design, wrong randomisation unit, predictable assignment, unrepresentative eligibility, and a primary metric weakly tied to value.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Audit the experiment as a causal system
turns.text: What changes when we look at audit the experiment as a causal system?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: During execution, watch for:

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: sample-ratio mismatch (SRM), where observed assignment counts differ implausibly from configuration; treatment and control implementation differences beyond the intended change; inconsistent triggering or exposure; missing, duplicated, or variant-specific events; bots, internal traffic, and identity failures; interference, leakage, or users switching variants; outages, seasonality, campaigns, policy shifts, and concurrent experiments; novelty, learning, and carryover effects.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: During analysis, threats include repeated peeking and stopping, outcome switching, unadjusted multiple comparisons, selective segments, inappropriate independence assumptions, outlier handling chosen after results, and confusing statistical with practical significance.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: After analysis, teams can still overgeneralise, ignore concentrated harm, mistake a proxy for value, or tell a causal mechanism the experiment did not test.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at trust checks precede product interpretation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Use A/A tests to evaluate platform false-positive behaviour, assignment, and metric variance. Monitor SRM and other invariants independently of outcome. Reconcile critical events against source-of-truth operational data. Compare logging schemas and event volumes by variant. Validate exposure and eligibility. Inspect time series for implementation changes and novelty.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Pre-specify primary metrics, guardrails, decision thresholds, duration, exclusions, and planned segments. Report confidence intervals, absolute effects, baselines, and practical significance. Preserve reproducible queries, code versions, experiment configuration, and anomalies.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Twyman’s Law offers a useful posture: any figure that looks unusually interesting or different is usually wrong. It is not a reason to dismiss discovery; it is a reason to investigate surprising wins as rigorously as losses.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: checkout “lift”?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A new checkout logs completion on button press while control logs confirmed payment. It reports a 4% lift. Order reconciliation removes the gain. The experiment process did not fail by rejecting the result; its quality system succeeded. Without source reconciliation, statistical machinery would have made a logging defect persuasive.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: A valid estimate can support a bad decision
turns.text: What changes when we look at a valid estimate can support a bad decision?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Even perfect randomisation cannot rescue a gameable OEC. A prompt can increase clicks by making the old path harder. Short-term activity may rise through novelty and later reverse. Aggregate improvement may hide harm to a smaller population. Interference may make treatment beneficial only while few users receive it.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The causal estimate must still be interpreted through product, ethical, and operational judgement.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at where this can go wrong?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: SRM dismissal: imbalance is treated as ordinary noise. Variant-specific telemetry: the treatment changes measurement as well as experience. Peeking and stopping: chance determines experiment duration. Multiplicity fishing: one favourable result is selected from many tests. Novelty permanence: initial curiosity is projected into durable behaviour.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Proxy win: target movement replaces user value. Clean-story pressure: inconvenient anomalies disappear from the decision record.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Audit the path from assignment to claim
turns.text: What changes when we look at audit the path from assignment to claim?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: He checks whether patients can encounter both variants across devices, whether staff behavior changes because they know the experiment, whether clinic capacity creates spillovers, and whether late outcomes are censored. A lift in “transfer requests” may reflect easier accidental activation; a reduction in support contacts may hide people who gave up.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Guardrails and qualitative follow-up test these explanations.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The team keeps an experiment log with hypothesis, pre-specified analysis, implementation checks, deviations, null findings, and decision. Results are reported with effect size, uncertainty interval, population, duration, and limitations. A clean number is not automatically credible; credibility comes from the design and the inspectable chain behind it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the harder design decision appear?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Create authority to invalidate results even when they support an executive preference. Separate experimentation platform health from team performance so people are rewarded for finding defects. High-stakes or surprising results deserve replication, longer follow-up, independent review, and mechanism evidence. An organisation that only celebrates wins will manufacture them.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Audit the path from assignment to conclusion
turns.text: What changes when we look at audit the path from assignment to conclusion?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A higher transfer-submission rate could reflect better comprehension, hidden consequences, or unsuitable requests. The team reviews appropriate resolution and safety guardrails, segments only with justified hypotheses, and reports uncertainty and practical effect.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Stopping rules and exclusions are defined in advance; surprising findings are treated as new hypotheses unless independently confirmed.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: <! -- Editorial: manual revision; curated product example --

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can we see that in a concrete product situation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Illustrative scenario: a donation page. A test appears to lift donations, but the variant ran mostly during a campaign while the control saw quieter days. Before trusting the result, examine assignment, exposure, sample ratio, instrumentation, repeated peeking, and whether one large gift drove the average. A clean-looking dashboard can still reflect a broken comparison.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should I notice the next time I use a product?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: When you see an unusually large experiment lift, write five non-product explanations. What invariant, source-of-truth comparison, or follow-up would test each one?
